title: Before a word is spoken, the coffee speaks.
content_en: The story of Saudi coffee in five short chapters: the sound that welcomes a guest, where coffee comes from, its tools, its customs, and how the world came to honor it.
content_ar: حكاية القهوة السعودية في خمسة فصول قصيرة: الصوت اللي يرحّب بالضيف، ومن وين جات القهوة، وعدّتها، وسلومها، وكيف صار العالم يعرفها.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Before a word is spoken, the coffee speaks."; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: The sound of the najr
content_en: For the people of Najd, coffee is the sign of generosity and the first thing offered to a guest. Its aroma fills the majlis before it is poured, and the ringing of the najr tells the neighbors that the house has a guest.
content_ar: القهوة عند أهل نجد عنوان الكرم وأول ما يُقدَّم للضيف. يفوح ريحها في المجلس قبل ما تنصب، وصوت النجر يعلن للجيران إن عند البيت ضيف.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "The sound of the najr"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Where coffee comes from
content_en: Most historians trace coffee from Ethiopia to Yemen, and from there to Makkah around the year 1500, from where it spread across Arabia. Saudi Arabia grows its own, too. On the terraced mountains of Jazan, 1,000 to 1,800 meters up, the farmers of Khawlan have grown the Khawlani coffee bean for more than 300 years.
content_ar: يرجّح أغلب المؤرخين إن القهوة انتقلت من الحبشة إلى اليمن، ومنها وصلت مكة المكرمة حوالي سنة ١٥٠٠م، وانتشرت في الجزيرة العربية. والسعودية تزرع قهوتها بعد: في جبال جازان، على مدرّجات ترتفع من ألف إلى ألف وثمانمية متر، يزرع أهل خولان البن الخولاني من أكثر من ٣٠٠ سنة.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Where coffee comes from"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: The tools of the coffee
content_en: In a Najdi majlis, the same set of tools waits by the fire. Tap each one to learn its name.
content_ar: في المجلس النجدي، نفس العدّة دايم جنب النار. اضغط على كل وحدة وتعرّف عليها.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "The tools of the coffee"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Mihmas
content_en: A shallow iron pan with a long handle. The green beans are roasted in it over the fire.
content_ar: مقلاة حديد بيد طويلة، يتحمّس فيها البن الأخضر على النار.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Al-Mihmas"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Mabrada
content_en: A tray of local wood where the roasted beans are spread out to cool before they are pounded.
content_ar: صحن من الخشب ينفرش فيه البن بعد التحميص عشان يبرد قبل الدق.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Al-Mabrada"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Najr
content_en: A brass mortar and pestle for pounding the beans. Its ringing tells the neighbors there is a guest.
content_ar: هاون نحاس مع يده، يندق فيه البن، ورنّته تعلم الجيران إن فيه ضيف.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Al-Najr"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Dallah
content_en: The coffee pot. A plug of palm fiber in its spout, the leef, keeps the grounds out of the cup.
content_ar: إبريق القهوة. وفي خشمها «الليف» اللي يمنع البن ينزل بالفنجال.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Al-Dallah"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: The customs of the cup
content_en: The server holds the dallah in his left hand and the cups in his right. He pours the first cup for the host, then serves the elders and the guests. The cup is filled only about a quarter, and refilled. When a guest has had enough, he shakes the cup as he hands it back.
content_ar: يمسك المُقهوي الدلة باليد اليسرى والفناجيل باليمنى، ويصب أول فنجال للمضيف، ثم يقدّم القهوة لكبار السن والضيوف. والفنجال ما ينملى، ربعه بس، وينعاد له. وإذا اكتفى الضيف هزّ الفنجال وهو يرجّعه.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "The customs of the cup"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Haif
content_en: The host drinks the first cup himself, so his guest knows the coffee is good.
content_ar: يشربه المضيف بنفسه، عشان يطمّن ضيفه إن القهوة زينة.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Al-Haif"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Dayf
content_en: The guest's cup, the duty of hospitality. A guest is expected to drink it.
content_ar: فنجال الضيف، واجب الضيافة، والضيف يشربه.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Al-Dayf"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Sayf
content_en: The cup of the sword. In old custom, drinking it meant standing with the host in hard times.
content_ar: فنجال السيف، وكان في السلوم القديمة يعني إن الضيف يوقف مع المضيف في الشدايد.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Al-Sayf"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: A heritage the world recognizes
content_en: UNESCO inscribed "Arabic coffee, a symbol of generosity" on its list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity, nominated by Saudi Arabia with the UAE, Oman, and Qatar.
content_ar: سجّلت اليونسكو «القهوة العربية، رمز الكرم» في قائمة التراث الثقافي غير المادي للبشرية، بترشيح من السعودية مع الإمارات وعُمان وقطر.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "A heritage the world recognizes"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: A heritage the world recognizes
content_en: The Ministry of Culture named 2022 the Year of Saudi Coffee, and the name "Saudi coffee" was adopted in cafés and restaurants across the Kingdom.
content_ar: أعلنت وزارة الثقافة ٢٠٢٢ «عام القهوة السعودية»، واعتُمد اسم «القهوة السعودية» في المقاهي والمطاعم بالمملكة.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "A heritage the world recognizes"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: A heritage the world recognizes
content_en: UNESCO inscribed the knowledge and practices of growing Khawlani coffee beans in Jazan.
content_ar: سجّلت اليونسكو المعارف والممارسات المرتبطة بزراعة البن الخولاني في جازان.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "A heritage the world recognizes"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Roast the beans
content_en: Roast the green beans in the mihmas over the fire, stirring, until they turn golden. Hold the button to roast, and let go when the color is right.
content_ar: حمّس البن الأخضر بالمحماس على النار وحرّكه لين يصير لونه ذهبي. اضغط مطوّل على الزر، وفكّه لما يصير اللون مضبوط.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Roast the beans"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Roast the beans
content_en: In Najd the roast is light and golden, never dark. A roasted batch is called a hamsa.
content_ar: في نجد التحميصة خفيفة ذهبية، مو غامقة. والكمية المحمّسة تسمى «حمسة».
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Roast the beans"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Pound it in the najr
content_en: The najr is struck in a rhythm, and its ringing tells the neighbors there is a guest.
content_ar: النجر ينطرق على إيقاع، ورنّته تعلم الجيران إن عندكم ضيف.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Pound it in the najr"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Boil the water
content_en: Pour water into the dallah and set it on the fire until it boils. Put the dallah on your table in AR and walk around it.
content_ar: حط الماي بالدلة وخلها على النار لين يغلي. حط الدلة على طاولتك بالواقع المعزز ولف حولها.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Boil the water"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Add the coffee
content_en: Add the ground coffee to the boiling water, about two to three tablespoons for three cups.
content_ar: حط البن المدقوق على الماي اللي يغلي، حوالي ملعقتين لثلاث ملاعق لكل ثلاث فناجيل.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Add the coffee"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Add the spices
content_en: Take the dallah off the fire and add crushed cardamom. In Najd, cloves and saffron are added too. Pick what goes in.
content_ar: شيل الدلة عن النار وزيد الهيل المدقوق، وفي نجد يزيدون القرنفل والزعفران. اختار وش يدخل فيها.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Add the spices"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Add the spices
content_en: Cardamom goes into every Saudi coffee. Each region adds its own touch: saffron in the east, mastic in the west.
content_ar: الهيل أساس القهوة السعودية، وكل منطقة لها لمستها: الزعفران في الشرقية، والمستكة في الغربية.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Add the spices"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Let it settle
content_en: The leef in the spout catches what is left, so only clear coffee reaches the cup.
content_ar: الليف اللي بخشم الدلة يمسك الباقي، فما يوصل الفنجال إلا القهوة الصافية.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Let it settle"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Sugar
content_en: No sugar. Saudi coffee is never sweetened; the dates bring the sweetness.
content_ar: لا سكر. القهوة السعودية ما تنحلّى، والتمر هو اللي يحلّيها.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Sugar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: Four men are seated in your majlis. Serve them the Najdi way: the right order, the right hand, the right amount. Then watch their cups.
content_ar: أربعة رجال جالسين بمجلسك. صب لهم على السلوم النجدية: بالترتيب الصح، وباليد الصح، وبالمقدار الصح. وبعدين انتبه لفناجيلهم.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: Right. The first cup, the haif, goes to the host. He tastes it so his guests know the coffee is good.
content_ar: صح. أول فنجال، الهيف، للمضيف. يذوقه عشان يطمّن ضيوفه إن القهوة زينة.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: Not yet. The first cup is the haif, and it goes to the host, Abu Fahad. He tastes it before anyone else.
content_ar: مو هو. أول فنجال هو الهيف، وهو للمضيف أبو فهد. يذوقه قبل الكل.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: The finjan is always offered with the right hand. The dallah stays in the left.
content_ar: الفنجال دايم ينعطى باليمين، والدلة تبقى باليسار.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: Too full. A full cup rushes the guest. A little at a time keeps him company.
content_ar: مليان زيادة. الفنجال المترّس كأنك تستعجل ضيفك، والقليل يونّسه.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: Right. He held it out without shaking it, so he would like more. This one is the kayf, the cup for pleasure.
content_ar: صح. مدّه بدون ما يهزه، يعني يبي زيادة. وهذا فنجال الكيف.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: Good. Cardamom is the heart of it. In Najd, cloves and saffron are often added too.
content_ar: زين. الهيل أساسها، وفي نجد غالباً يزيدون القرنفل والزعفران.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Omar
content_en: You roasted it, pounded it, brewed it, and spiced it the Najdi way. Now the most important part: serving it.
content_ar: حمّستها، ودقّيتها، وطبختها، وهيّلتها على الطريقة النجدية. والحين أهم شي: الصبّة.
source: CultureLens, qahwa chapter "Omar"; sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage lists; Saudi Ministry of Culture; Ajel and Riyadh Daily, on the coffee tools (2026); the CultureLens heritage sheet

title: Al-Samri
content_en: A night art from Najd: two rows that answer each other in song, the beat of the drums, and bodies swaying as one. Its name comes from samar, staying up late talking at night.
content_ar: فن ليلي من نجد: صفّان يرد واحدهم على الثاني بالغناء، مع قرع الطبول، وأجساد تتمايل كأنها وحدة. واسمه من «السَّمَر»، وهو السهر والحديث بالليل.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Al-Samri"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: From Al-Qassim across the Kingdom
content_en: It began in Al-Qassim and grew in Najd, then spread to Hail, Wadi Al-Dawasir, Al-Jawf, Riyadh and beyond, each place with its own melody.
content_ar: بدأ من القصيم وازدهر في نجد، وانتشر لحائل ووادي الدواسر والجوف والرياض وغيرها، ولكل مكان لحنه.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "From Al-Qassim across the Kingdom"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Unaizah
content_en: Its Samri is the best known: slow, heavy, and unlike any other. Its men gathered every Thursday night, and in summer they met out in the sand dunes beyond the town.
content_ar: سامريها الأشهر: ثقيل وبطيء وما يشبه غيره. رجالها يجتمعون كل ليلة جمعة، وبالصيف يلتقون في النفود برّا البلد.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Unaizah"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Al-Jawf
content_en: The poet sings the poem out loud, and the two facing rows repeat it, taking turns on the drums.
content_ar: الشاعر ينشد القصيدة بصوت عالي، والصفّان المتقابلان يرددونها ويتناوبون ضرب الدفوف.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Al-Jawf"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Two rows, face to face
content_en: Two rows of men kneel facing each other, eight to ten in a row at first and many more today. Each row has an expert leader, the mu'allim, at its center. Beginners start at the ends and move toward the center as they learn.
content_ar: يجثو صفّان من الرجال متقابلين، كان الصف من ثمانية لعشرة، واليوم أكثر بكثير. ولكل صف معلّم خبير بنصّه. والمبتدئ يبدأ من طرف الصف، ويقرب للنص كل ما تعلّم.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Two rows, face to face"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: The drum
content_en: The tar is a wooden frame with goat or sheep skin stretched over it. The skin is tightened until it gives the sound they want, and if it gets too tight, it is moistened with water.
content_ar: الطار إطار من الخشب مشدود عليه جلد ماعز أو غنم. يُشد الجلد لين يعطي الصوت المطلوب، وإذا صار مشدود زيادة يُرطّب بالماء.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "The drum"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: The drum
content_en: In Unaizah the beat is slow and heavy: one stroke on its own, then three in a row. The light Samri of the rest of Najd is fast: two strokes in a row, then one. A big frame drum, the marjaf, makes the beat stronger.
content_ar: في عنيزة الإيقاع ثقيل وبطيء: ضربة لحالها، وبعدها ثلاث ضربات ورا بعض. أما السامري الخفيف في باقي نجد فسريع: ضربتين ورا بعض، وبعدها ضربة وحدة. وفيه طار كبير اسمه «المرجاف» يقوّي الإيقاع.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "The drum"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Poetry that answers itself
content_en: The leader calls and the rows line up, and the waneen opens the night with a tune. Then the first row sings a line of the poem (they call it yisheel) and the second sings it back, which is why it is called the marrad. The leader keeps feeding them the verses.
content_ar: ينادي قائد الفرقة فيتراص الصفّان، ويبدأ «الونين» وهو الافتتاحية. وبعدين الصف الأول «يشيل» البيت والثاني يرده، وعشان كذا اسمه «المرد». والقائد أو «الملقّن» يلقّنهم أبيات القصيدة.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Poetry that answers itself"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Poetry that answers itself
content_en: Every first half of a verse ends on one rhyme and every second half on another, like -ūnī and -rā here. The poems speak of love, longing, praise and parting, and Muhsin Al-Hazzani of Najd is named among the first Samri poets.
content_ar: كل صدر بيت ينتهي بقافية، وكل عجز بقافية ثانية، مثل «ـوني» و«ـرا» هنا. والقصايد عن الحب والشوق والمدح والفراق، ومن أوائل شعراء السامري محسن الهزاني من نجد.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Poetry that answers itself"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: A Samri on any topic
content_en: Pick a topic and hear a Samri the AI wrote on it: two verses in the meter of the verse you just heard, with one rhyme for the first halves and another for the second. The first row carries each verse and the second sings it back.
content_ar: اختر موضوع واسمع سامري كتبه عليه الذكاء الاصطناعي: بيتين بنفس وزن البيت اللي سمعته، بقافية للصدور وقافية للأعجاز. الصف الأول يشيل البيت والثاني يرده.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "A Samri on any topic"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Still sung today
content_en: Unaizah still holds Samri evenings every week, kept up by its young men and its elders.
content_ar: ما زالت عنيزة تقيم حفلات السامري كل أسبوع، يحييها شبابها وكبارها.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Still sung today"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Still sung today
content_en: The Ministry of Culture listed Samri among the folk arts of its national cultural competitions.
content_ar: أدرجت وزارة الثقافة السامري ضمن الفنون الشعبية في مسابقاتها الثقافية الوطنية.
source: CultureLens, samri chapter "Still sung today"; sources: Aramco World (2007); the Samri booklet of Wrth; Saudipedia; Abdulaziz Al-Qadi, "Samri Unaizah", Al-Jazirah (2025)

title: Still sung today
content_en: It is a fixture of National Day, Souq Okaz and the Janadriyah festival.
content_ar: وصار حاضر في اليوم الوطني وسوق عكاظ ومهرجان الجنادرية.
